question.problem: Express $\sqrt{\frac{m+10}{m-10}}\,$ without radicals in the denominator.
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{m+10}{m-10}} & =\frac{\sqrt{m+10}}{\sqrt{m-10}}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the radical $\sqrt{m-10}$ from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{m-10}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{m+10}}{\sqrt{m-10}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{m+10}}{\sqrt{m-10}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{m-10}}{\sqrt{m-10}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{m+10}\cdot \sqrt{m-10}}{\sqrt{m-10}\cdot \sqrt{m-10}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{(m+10)(m-10)}}{(\sqrt{m-10})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{{m}^{2}-{10}^{2}}}{m-10} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{{m}^{2}-100}}{m-10}\end{aligned}
$$
